observations.text: Complete Sweep sources include explicit refusal for both increased and decreased native balances, a delayed balance-read change, same-nonce replacement binding, and a deposit after the checked snapshot. Native fee review tests bind the final serialized transaction to the public balance/fees/net shown before separate confirmation and refuse changed fee/balance data. These support the existing PN-02 candidate disposition; assertions were read, not executed.

Helper tests reject revoked direct and relayed reviews before derivation, across awaited RPC/signature steps, and before handoff; preserve submitted or uncertain outcomes after transport starts. Native confirmation tests cover copied reviews, changed fields, clock rollback/expiry, cancellation, session replacement and concurrent confirmation. Quote lifecycle view tests exercise destination, balance, endpoint, mode and selection changes while vault/RPC/helper work is pending, including same-nonce replacements and retention of prior hashes. This supplements PN-03 without adding a new defect or runtime claim.

Boundary tests use real cryptographic implementations and the actual RPC client/network-authority adapter around synthetic transport to check late revocation and conservative unknown-outcome journaling. Journal and UI tests cover malformed/unavailable persistence, pre-handoff write failure, all hashes from same-nonce replacements, exact-hash receipt reconciliation, finalized nonce replacement, and relayed-order nonce/deadline reconciliation. Full review establishes what the test assertions specify; no tests were run.

The older privacy test blob explicitly expects automatic Settings-RPC balance reads outside required local-proxy mode. The candidate-aligned blob expects an explicit click in all modes and covers pending-read invalidation without fallback. Destination-link tests require session-only history, removal without import of the legacy plaintext key, clearing on lock/session change, and refusal of delayed completion to repopulate it. These are exact snapshot differences, not a claim that sibling branches contain candidate fixes.

Two legacy helper test titles overstate their individual assertions. The relayed failure test titled as wiping the stealth key only asserts promise rejection and does not observe the derived buffer. The feeTo-review test passes the correct manifest fee recipient and fails because the permit RPC mock always throws, so that particular assertion does not exercise fee-recipient mismatch. A separate case at 110-134 explicitly rejects a mismatched recipient, so this is not a claim that fee-recipient protection is globally untested. Strengthen the named tests with direct zeroization/specific-refusal assertions or rename them to their actual scope. No production defect is inferred.
